structure: Part 12, the transporter list and choosing a transporter. Read in full, from repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend (HEAD on main): the transport feature's page.js (6 page records, of which transportersPage and transporterAddPage are this part's); transporters/ in full apart from its *.test.js unit tests (transporters.controller.js, transporters.njk, _cells.njk, rows.js, validate.js, transporter-record.js); transporter-add/ in full apart from its unit test (transporter-add.controller.js, transporter-add.njk); the feature-level transporter-add-session.js, own-transporter-type.js and test-support.js; transport/copy/copy.en.js in full, with the transporters and transporterAdd branches claimed string by string and copy.cy.js read for key parity over those same branches; fit/transporters.fit.spec.js (1,508 lines, 11 describes) with only the tests about the list, the type question and the add choice claimed, the two details forms left to part 13; and the client-side src/client/javascripts/components/transporter-filter.js. Covered: two pages — the transporter list at /notifications/{journeyId}/transporters (H1 'Transporter details', intro, DAERA/APHA authorisation guidance with its three conditions and GOV.UK link, an H2 'Select a transporter', a server-and-client search with an Add a transporter button beside it, and a seven-column radio table of the organisation's transporters with status tags and a View details link into the INS address book) and the transporter type question at /notifications/{journeyId}/transporters/add (H1 'Choose a transporter type', a duplicate-check warning, two radios Private and Commercial, Continue, branching to transporters/add/private or transporters/add/commercial). Also covered: every validation message on both pages verbatim, the added-transporter success banner, the flow-only session keys that carry an in-progress add, the redirect that keeps a details form to its own type, and what the fit spec proves about all of this with JavaScript on and off. Not covered here: the two details forms themselves (part 13), the port-of-entry and transit-countries pages in the same feature and copy file (other parts), and the Welsh strings themselves.
